pairs.subject: sidecar-provisioning
pairs.evidence: src/features/plugins/dev-tools/sub_skills/analytics/StaticScanConfigModal.tsx:25 The shipped default static-scan command runs an unpinned `npx fallow`, so each run executes whatever npm currently resolves for that name: no catalog entry, no version pin, no content check before the bytes run.

techniques.evidence: src/features/plugins/dev-tools/sub_skills/analytics/StaticScanConfigModal.tsx:25 Default argv fetches and runs an npm package with no version or digest pinned. The `impeccable` default at :29 (`npx impeccable detect --json --no-advisory src`) has the same gap, and the comment at :26 presents 'npx on demand' as the whole setup.

pairs.registryProposal: Source-pinning names libraries that provision themselves, but not a user-editable default command that fetches through a package runner (npx/uvx/pipx). That door is common in dev-tool hosts and could be named as its own case.

pairs.subject: sidecar-provisioning
pairs.evidence: src/features/overview/components/health/SystemHealthPanel.tsx:58 The panel destructures only `install` from useAutoInstaller, which also exports `cancel` (useAutoInstaller.ts:176), so a running Node/Claude CLI download or install has no way to be cancelled from this surface.

techniques.evidence: src/features/overview/components/health/InstallButton.tsx:38 While downloading or installing, the only thing rendered is a progress strip plus the last output line. There is no cancel control, although the hook has one. The technique treats cancellation as a first-class exit.

src/features/overview/components/health/InstallButton.tsx:33 Any status other than ok gets the same 'Install' remedy. The backend tells broken apart from absent (health.rs: Warn 'detected in PATH, but version probe failed' vs Error 'Not found', both installable:true), but here both become one Install button, which tells a user who already has it installed to install it. In its favour: the verdict is re-run after an install completes (SystemHealthPanel.tsx:77 runSection('environment')).
